# Swellfire Marketing & Store Media — Design

**Date:** 2026-05-29
**Status:** Approved (design phase)
**Goal:** Build, for Swellfire, the full media set CoinTex has — generated by reproducible
tooling wherever CoinTex used tooling — and commit it under `swellfire_media/`.

## Background

Swellfire (formerly GateRunner) is a Kivy auto-runner squad-shooter: the player drags to
steer a squad that **swells** through math gates (`×2`, `+5`, …) and auto-**fires** at
enemies; each of 6 worlds (10 levels each, 60 total) ends in a boss. The game renders at a
logical 960×540 (16:9), pixel-art sprites with `nearest` filtering, music per world + boss,
and a GA autoplayer (`autoplay.py`) that can drive the squad autonomously.

CoinTex's media set (the target to mirror), all in `cointex_media/`:
- `cointex_logo.png` 512×512 (launcher/window icon) + `cointex_presplash.png` (splash).
- 8 phone screenshots @1280×720 + 8 tablet screenshots @1920×1080 (`tablet_screenshots/`).
- `feature_graphic_1024x500.png` (Google Play banner).
- `youtube_thumbnail_1280x720.png` (YouTube cover).
- 3 videos: a promo (~2 MB), a long autoplay-with-SFX clip (1080p), a vertical short (Reels).
- Generated by reproducible PIL tools: `gen_assets.py`, `make_feature_graphic.py`,
  `make_youtube_thumbnail.py`, `upscale_screenshots.py`. Videos were made externally (no tooling).
- Window/desktop icon set in code via `self.icon` + `Window.set_icon(...)`.

Swellfire today: `icon.png` (512×512) and `presplash.png` (1920×1080) exist but are explicit
**placeholders** ("GR / PLACEHOLDER / replaced in M14", still branded "GateRunner"). No window
icon wired in `main.py`. No marketing media. `tools/` already has audio/atlas/sprite generators.

## Decisions (locked)

- **Brand direction:** *Ember* (fire-forward). Palette: `#160604` ember-black, `#7a0d12`
  blood, `#d61f1f` red, `#ff7a18` orange, `#ffd34d` gold; squad accents in cream/cool-gold.
- **Logo glyph:** a squad chevron (three runners in a V) bursting upward out of a flame, with
  a small `×2` gate tab. Wordmark "**Swell**fire" (gold/white split).
- **Tagline:** "Grow your squad. Open fire." Info line: "60 levels · 6 worlds · 2-player versus".
- **Video capture:** deterministic offline render (capture mode + fixed-dt sim + framebuffer
  grab + event-logged audio rebuilt from the game's own WAVs + ffmpeg mux). Not live screen-grab.
- **Long autoplay coverage:** per world, **1 early level + that world's boss** → 12 segments,
  all 6 bosses shown.
- **Video resolution:** **1920×1080 (1080p Full HD)** for promo + long autoplay. Vertical short
  is 1080×1920 (9:16).
- **ffmpeg:** `imageio-ffmpeg` (bundled static binary, pip-installed into the venv, **no sudo**),
  used as a **dev/build-time** tool only — like numpy, never a runtime/mobile dependency.

## Architecture

### Brand graphics (PIL, deterministic)
Three self-contained PIL scripts, seeded RNG for reproducible bokeh/embers, font fallback
(DejaVuSans-Bold). Shared `Ember` palette + a small helper to draw the squad-chevron-in-flame
glyph and the "Swellfire" wordmark, so logo/presplash/feature/thumbnail stay visually unified.
- `tools/gen_brand_assets.py`: `make_icon()` (512×512, rounded square, glyph), `make_presplash()`
  (1920×1080, glyph + wordmark + tagline on ember gradient). Writes repo-root `icon.png`,
  `presplash.png` and copies into `swellfire_media/`.
- `tools/make_feature_graphic.py`: 1024×500 banner — ember gradient, glow, ember-bokeh, squad of
  runners + a boss silhouette + glowing gates, title + tagline + info line.
- `tools/make_youtube_thumbnail.py`: 1280×720 — high-energy action scene (squad firing right,
  boss looming, muzzle flashes, glowing `×2`/`+5` gates), bold title, tagline, motion streaks.

### Capture system (engine for screenshots + video)
- **Capture mode** toggled by env `SWELLFIRE_CAPTURE` (kept out of the normal run path). When on:
  - the GA autoplayer is driven **inline** off the sim clock (no wall-clock daemon thread), so
    runs are repeatable;
  - the sim advances at **fixed dt = 1/60 s** regardless of real frame time;
  - after each rendered frame, the GL framebuffer is read (`glReadPixels` via a post-draw hook,
    e.g. `Window.on_flip` / a low-priority Clock callback) into a numpy array and either written
    as a PNG or fed to the frame sink.
- **Audio timeline:** `audio.AudioManager.play_sfx` / music-switch calls append
  `(sim_time, kind, name)` to an in-memory log when capture mode is on; flushed to JSON per clip.
- `tools/capture.py`: a thin harness/CLI that boots the app in capture mode, navigates to a target
  (a specific screen for screenshots, or a level/boss for video segments), runs N frames, and
  emits frames + the audio-event JSON. Reused by both the screenshot and video steps.
- `tools/mix_audio.py`: given an audio-event JSON + the segment's world, builds a WAV soundtrack —
  the correct looping music bed (menu/world1..6/boss) under SFX one-shots overlaid at their
  timestamps. Continuous/high-rate cues (`shoot`) are rate-limited so the mix stays musical, per
  the game's own SFX-restraint rule. Pure numpy + stdlib `wave`.
- `tools/make_videos.py`: orchestrates segment capture → audio mix → ffmpeg encode (H.264 + AAC)
  → concatenation/compositing into the three final videos. Uses `imageio_ffmpeg.get_ffmpeg_exe()`.

### Screenshots
8 scenes captured through the harness: (1) title, (2) world map, (3) level select,
(4) gameplay with gates swelling the squad, (5) boss fight, (6) level-complete + stars,
(7) shop, (8) guide/tutorial. Captured at 1280×720, then `upscale_screenshots.py` LANCZOS-upscales
to 1920×1080 tablet copies — identical pipeline and framing to CoinTex.

### Videos
- **Long autoplay** (`swellfire_autoplay_1080p.mp4`, 1080p): 12 segments (early level + boss per
  world), each trimmed to a highlight window; intro/outro title cards; per-world lower-third
  label; world music follows the world, boss music on bosses; SFX overlaid from the event log.
- **Promo** (`swellfire_promo.mp4`, 1080p, ~45–60 s): fast-cut highlight montage (gate-swell,
  combat, a boss kill, stars) with a title-card intro and an end card (logo + tagline + info
  line); SFX hits synced to cuts.
- **Vertical short** (`swellfire_short_vertical.mp4`, 1080×1920, ~20–30 s): punchiest swell +
  boss-kill moments composed into an Ember vertical frame (gameplay in a centered 16:9 band,
  ember background, bold top/bottom captions); music + key SFX.

### Window icon wiring
In `main.py` `SwellfireApp.build()`: resolve the icon via the existing frozen-aware `ASSET_ROOT`
(not `os.path.dirname(__file__)` — see CLAUDE.md packaged-path gotcha), then set `self.icon` and
call `Window.set_icon(path)` if the file exists (silent skip otherwise). Result: the Ember icon
shows in the window's top-left and is used by the Linux/Windows/macOS desktop builds (PyInstaller
already passes `icon.png`).

### Packaging / housekeeping
- `swellfire_media/` added to `buildozer.spec` `source.exclude_dirs` (don't ship marketing media).
- `imageio-ffmpeg` documented as a dev/build dependency (e.g. `requirements-dev.txt` or a tools
  README note), explicitly not in `buildozer.spec requirements`.
- README/CLAUDE.md note on how to regenerate each media artifact.

## Testing / verification

- **Brand graphics:** assert each generator writes a file of the exact expected dimensions and
  mode; eyeball the rendered PNGs (sent to the user) and iterate on the Ember art.
- **Capture frame-grab (highest risk):** prototype first — capture a 1-second gameplay clip and
  confirm non-blank, correctly-sized frames before building the rest.
- **Audio mix:** assert the mixed WAV duration matches the segment frame count / fps; spot-check
  that logged SFX appear at the right offsets.
- **Videos:** ffprobe each output for resolution (1920×1080 / 1080×1920), an audio stream present,
  and expected duration; watch them.
- **Window icon:** launch `SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy venv/bin/python main.py` and confirm the icon in
  the title bar; smoke-test a packaged build from a foreign cwd (CLAUDE.md rule).
- **No regressions:** capture mode is gated behind an env flag; the normal game path is unchanged.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Kivy framebuffer grab** may need the right post-draw hook / a real GL context (we have a
  display). *Mitigation:* prototype the grab in isolation first; fall back to `Window.screenshot`
  if `glReadPixels` is awkward.
- **Autoplayer inline determinism:** decisions currently run on a wall-clock thread. *Mitigation:*
  drive `sense`/`_decide` inline off the sim clock in capture mode only.
- **Video length / encode time:** 12 segments × highlight windows. *Mitigation:* per-segment
  highlight trims; capture is decoupled from real time so quality is unaffected by encode speed.

## Out of scope

- New gameplay/art beyond what's needed to frame good screenshots.
- App-store listing copy, localization, ASO.
- iOS icon-set application (`ios_apply_assets.sh` equivalent) — can follow later if desired.
